subject: Delegated access & cross-border transfer runbook
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmehealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: 2026-08-16T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Runbook request — delegated access + transfers

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. AcmeHealth is finalizing the DPA annex for our pilot and our privacy team has a couple of practical asks before legal will sign:

1) A short operational runbook that shows how Redwood delegates access (per-account roles, temporary sessions) and the evidence we can provide at onboarding.
2) A clear mapping of which subprocessors handle identifiable data and where (e.g., US-east, EU, backups).
3) If there are any cross-border transfers, what controls we have (KMS custody, pseudonymization, contractual transfer mechanisms).

We usually accept a 1–2 page runbook + a subprocessor snapshot as part of the DPA annex. Can you share a draft and who on your side will own the evidence?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Daniel Park
Senior Privacy PM, AcmeHealth
privacy_team@acmehealth.com
[Attachment: privacy_template_questions.pdf]
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example, grace_oconnor@redwood.example
Date: 2026-08-16T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runbook request — delegated access + transfers

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi (legal) and Grace (security) who will help with the DPA language and evidence.

Quick answers up front:
- Owner for evidence: Marissa (onboarding) will operate the subprocessor snapshot and can generate an account-specific export.
- Cross-border transfers: Redwood routes customer data according to region rules, with KMS-backed keys per-customer where required; we can provide exportable KMS key custody attestations and a transfer map.

I attached an operational runbook draft and a current subprocessor snapshot for ACME to review — they're placeholders but should be close to what you asked for.

Do you have a target SLA for delivery of the annex (e.g., sign by EOW)? If so we can prioritize. Also, is there a specific format your legal/privacy team prefers for the subprocessor evidence (CSV vs signed attestations)?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example
Redwood Inference

Daniel / Stephanie — thanks. I reviewed Stephanie's draft runbook and added a few redlines for the DPA annex that should satisfy Acme's legal team while keeping our operational model intact. Key points in the redline:

- Subprocessor disclosure cadence: propose quarterly snapshot with the ability to provide on-request export within 5 business days.
- KMS custody: we confirm that for Private deployments and Dedicated contracts customers may manage their keys (BYOK); for Hosted customers we hold per-customer KMS keys in a multi-tenant HSM-backed service — we can provide key custody attestations +/- 30 days.
- Transfers: where transfers rely on standard contractual clauses we include a mapping table and the contract reference; where relying on adequacy decisions (EU -> US) we will call that out explicitly.

I attached the redline and a short clause you can paste into the annex. If Acme needs signed attestations for specific subprocessors (e.g., cloud backups), Marissa can surface those vendor confirmations.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redline_DPA_annex_stephanie_v1.docx]

Hi Daniel — fyi on the operational side:

- Subprocessor snapshot: I attached a CSV export with current subprocessors and location tags. For customer-specific exports we can filter by project and generate a signed snapshot within 3 business days.
- Evidence types: we can provide (a) vendor statements of processing, (b) SOC 2 in-scope description, and (c) signed subprocessor confirmations on request (these take longer). Which of these does Acme prefer?
- Access delegation: our platform issues short-lived service tokens for onboarding ops (default 1 hour), role-based session records are retained for 90 days in the audit log. We can export a per-account audit-tail for the time window you specify.

Next steps I propose:
1) Acme confirms which evidence (CSV snapshot vs signed attestations) they need for the DPA annex.
2) If needed, schedule a 30min run-through with our security engineer (Grace) to walk the runbook.
3) Rishi will share the annex redline we discussed.

Attachments: subprocessor_snapshot_20260816.csv (already attached), runbook_v1.pdf (Stephanie's draft).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Onboarding Manager, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Acme's privacy team is comfortable with the CSV snapshot + per-account audit tail to start; for a small number of subprocessors we will request signed confirmations later in the week.

We want the following deliverables before our legal sign-off:
- Finalized runbook (1–2 pages) with a short dataflow diagram attached.
- Subprocessor CSV export filtered to our account.
- KMS custody statement (custody + BYOK options) and the DPA annex redline you suggested.

Can we aim to have those by EOD Friday (2026-08-20)? If so I will coordinate legal to be available for a short review call. Otherwise propose next Tuesday.

Thanks — Daniel
